top_signals.title: Big Oil and Big Tech Lobby EU for Faster Gas-Fired Data Center Permits
top_signals.summary: Kazakhstan has joined Iraq in asking OPEC+ to raise its estimate of the country's crude production capacity, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The request comes four days before the group meets to set its output policy for 2027. The review is OPEC's first, and will assess how much oil each member can produce sustainably, and its findings will help set production targets for next year. top_signals.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
top_signals.summary: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

top_signals.title: Why Is Thanksgiving So Expensive This Year?
top_signals.summary: Planning your Thanksgiving grocery run? You might notice a few changes in the aisles this year. From the disappearing “free turkey” promotion to milk prices jumping nearly 8%, Deena Shanker joins Max Chafkin on Everybody’s Business to unpack the real cost of Thanksgiving dinner—and what’s driving grocery prices right now. Listen to the full episode wherever you get your podcasts.  (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Almost 60% of primary energy used for electricity is lost to conversion and transmission
top_signals.summary: In 2025, the United States consumed 34 quadrillion British thermal units (quads) of primary energy to deliver 14 quads of electricity sales to end users, with nearly 60% lost. About 95% of the losses came from converting primary energy into electricity, mostly due to lost heat from burning coal and natural gas. The remaining 5% was lost in the course of delivering electricity across grid infrastructure to homes and businesses.
